title.narrative: Botswana Constitution Review Process: Towards a People Driven Constitution

description.narrative:
This Action is a collaborative initiative by Botswana Council of Non-Governmental Organisations (BOCONGO) as the Lead Applicant, Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS (BONELA), DITSHWANELO and Emang Basadi as Co-applicants respectively. The member organisations of BOCONGO led by the thematic groups and regional networks spread throughout the geographic regions of the country will participate as Affiliated Entities based on their competitive and complementary strengths. The Big Governance Issues In Botswana, A Civil Society Submission To The African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) Report compiled by civil society organisations in Botswana during the course of 2020 and 2021, guided by the South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA) and BOCONGO highlights consensus amongst Botswana civil society on key issues of concern which form the basis for priority setting for the Constitutional Review process. The issues include, Human Rights, Separation of Powers, Public Service and Decentralisation, Citizen Participation and Economic Inclusion, Transparency and Accountability, Vulnerable Groups, Education, Sustainable Development and Natural Resource Management, Access to Land and Infrastructure, Food Security, Crime and Security, Foreign Policy, Research and Development. 

However, recognising that the areas are too broad, they were further distilled and the consensus reached through consultation of broader civil society is that the proposed action should place premium focus on issues of gender equality and women in politics, the death penalty, debt cap, socio-economic and cultural rights,   The action places premium focus on prioritised areas of gender equality and women in politics, the death penalty, debt cap, socioeconomic and cultural rights, civic participation, democratic governance, and human rights.
